title: listScopeItems executes a batched query rather than one populate query per row for a 100-item scope page
description: Live defect M-004 (open): audit-assurance.controller.js listScopeItems (reported near lines 622-655) issues a per-item .populate() lookup instead of a single batched populate/$lookup, producing roughly 100 queries for a 100-item page.
preconditions: An audit has 100+ scope items, each with an assignee reference
steps: Enable MongoDB query logging (profiler level 1) or attach a query counter
Count the number of distinct queries issued for the request
expectedResult: Current behavior: query count scales roughly 1:1 with returned row count (~100 queries for 100 rows). Flag for remediation: replace the per-row lookup with a single populate() call or aggregation $lookup so query count stays constant regardless of page size.

title: Audit Trends (R21) and Continuous Improvement Dashboard (R22) aggregate endpoints have no pagination
description: Live defect M-011 (open): audit-trends.controller.js and continuous-improvement.controller.js aggregate queries return unbounded result sets with no page/limit enforcement.
preconditions: Org has 2+ years of audit history generating a large trends dataset
steps: Call the audit-trends-benchmarking report endpoint for an org with a large history
Call the continuous-improvement-dashboard report endpoint for the same org
Measure response payload size and server response time
expectedResult: Current behavior: both endpoints return the full unbounded dataset with no pagination, response size/time growing linearly with history depth. Flag for remediation: add page/limit or date-range bounding to both aggregate queries.

title: Findings list endpoint stays within SLA and enforces its 100-item page cap for an org with 10,000+ findings
preconditions: Org has 10,000+ finding/CAR documents in audit_nonconformances
steps: Call GET /:auditId/findings?limit=1000 against an org with a large finding volume
Measure response time and returned row count
expectedResult: The response is capped at 100 rows regardless of the requested limit (Math.min(100,...) at findings.controller.js:48) and completes within the module's defined P95 latency budget.

title: Concurrent escalate() triggers on a large overdue CAR set do not produce duplicate escalation writes
description: escalate() (corrective-action.service.js:862-908) loops over overdue CARs performing individual updateOne calls with no transaction; concurrent scheduler/cron triggers could double-write the same escalation event, though the resulting escalationLevel value itself is idempotent (same value written twice).
preconditions: 100+ CARs are overdue past the 'manager' escalation threshold
steps: Trigger POST /corrective-actions/escalate twice concurrently against the same org's overdue CAR set
expectedResult: escalationLevel converges to the same correct value for every CAR either way, but verify whether the activity log (logAuditActivity) records a duplicate escalation notification entry per CAR — if so, flag for remediation (wrap the batch in a transaction or de-duplicate by targetClosureDate/escalationLevel state).
